chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The time for the Maghrib prayer during travel extends until one-quarter of the night.'
ai.seo_question: What is the extended time for Maghrib prayer during travel according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) to clarify the extended window for Maghrib prayer during travel, a ruling derived from the ease (*rukhsah*) granted to travelers. This specific timeframe—until one-quarter of the night—reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that allows for the combination of Maghrib and Isha, accommodating the fatigue of the journey while maintaining the integrity of the prayer times.
